title: Zesty Smoky Russian Beef Pirozhki
description: A smoky and crunchy Russian dish featuring ground cardamom, perfect for a romantic dinner, this recipe is low-glycemic-friendly and made with wholesome ingredients. The combination of beef, spices, and flaky crust will leave you wanting more.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large skillet, cook the ground beef over medium-high heat until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper to the skillet and cook until the onion is translucent.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and a pinch of salt.
Add the cold unsalted butter to the bowl and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work it into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the beaten egg to the bowl, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together in a ball.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead it a few times until it becomes smooth and pliable.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle and place a tablespoon of the beef mixture in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-circle shape and press the edges together to seal the pirozhki.
Place the pirozhki on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush the tops with a little bit of water.
Bake the pirozhki in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
